analysis:
Documentation-only changes in docs/architecture/inference.md. Head lines 632-637 describe EnginePerformanceMeasurements.Rate freshness anchored to the newest observation, so out-of-order receipts cannot move freshness backward. Head lines 883-917 describe the TTFT admission estimator corrections: per-step decode pricing via CBv2DecodeRateShape, MTP depth-ceiling mirroring, and an idle-calibration floor on the prefill rate with a 30-minute expiry. The DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES=0 rollback is also documented. Base line 1736 and head line 1780 are outside the supplied units.

These are availability and routing-estimate semantics for the first-content deadline admission path (T-010/T-029 class). They do not touch encryption, attestation, authorization or cache scoping. The text states that physical admission, memory reservations and actual deadline expiry still apply, so an estimate error affects only admission optimism.

Cache-related prose in the unchanged context matches T-041 posture. Line 522 says Super's coordinator prefix reuse is partitioned by the authenticated cache scope. Line 807 covers the SSD stage. No contradiction with T-041 or SEC-035 was found.

Remaining unverified: the implementation in AdmissionRateEstimators.swift and EnginePerformanceMeasurements, which was not supplied. In particular, it is unconfirmed that the rollback environment variable is rejected by DeadlineRuntimeEnvironment.permitsQualification (line 948 says unrecognized DARKBLOOM_* settings are rejected). This is a qualification-integrity question, not a security regression.
